explanation.en: **Not only ... but also** joins two results of the tax, and the correct answer keeps both, including **more money than expected** and **Several** manufacturers.

items.stem: What turns flamingos pink is less their genes than the pigments in the algae and shrimp they eat, which is why captive birds deprived of such food gradually fade to a pallid white.
options: Flamingos' genes, rather than the pigments in the algae and shrimp they eat, are what mainly turn them pink, which is why captive birds keep their color even on a plain diet.
Flamingos owe their pink color more to pigments in the algae and shrimp in their diet than to their genes, so in captivity, without that food, they slowly turn a pale white.
Captive flamingos fade to a pallid white when zoos lack the funds to feed them the algae and shrimp whose pigments, rather than the birds' genes, are mainly what turns them pink.
Because captive flamingos lack the genes for pink pigment, they turn pale even when fed the algae and shrimp that their wild relatives eat.

explanation.he: המבנה **less their genes than the pigments** פירושו שהצבע תלוי יותר בפיגמנטים שבמזון מאשר בגנים, והתשובה הנכונה אומרת זאת בצירוף **more to pigments ... than to their genes** (יותר לפיגמנטים מאשר לגנים).
explanation.en: **less their genes than the pigments** means diet matters more than genes, which the correct answer keeps with **more to pigments ... than to their genes**.

items.stem: Little did the engineers who added a text-messaging function to early mobile phones suspect that a feature they regarded as a trifling extra would one day rival voice calls in popularity.
options: Although they considered texting a trifling extra, the engineers who installed it on early mobile phones had little doubt that one day it would rival voice calls in popularity.

Early mobile phones were given a texting function mainly to please the network operators, and the engineers who designed it, viewing the feature as an unimportant bonus, little suspected that the feature would one day be used as widely as voice calls.
Little did early mobile-phone users suspect that the engineers regarded text messaging as a trifling extra, since it soon rivaled voice calls in popularity.
The engineers who built texting into early mobile phones saw it as a minor add-on and had no idea that it would eventually become about as popular as voice calls.

explanation.he: המבנה **Little did ... suspect** פירושו שהמהנדסים כלל לא חשדו, והתשובה הנכונה שומרת על השלילה בצירוף **had no idea** (לא היה להם מושג).
explanation.en: **Little did ... suspect** means the engineers did not suspect at all, which the correct answer keeps with **had no idea**.

items.stem: Much as most internet users avow that their privacy matters to them, few are willing to pay even a small fee for a service that would keep their personal data out of advertisers' hands.
options: Few internet users are willing to pay even a small fee for a service that would keep their personal data out of advertisers' hands, because most of them avow that their privacy matters to them.
Much as most internet users claim to value their privacy, few will pay even a little to keep their personal data from advertisers, since they doubt that such services work.
Although the majority of internet users say they care about their privacy, only a handful would pay even a modest fee for a service that kept advertisers from getting their personal data.
Much as advertisers avow that they respect internet users' privacy, few of them are willing to pay even a small fee for the personal data they collect.

explanation.he: הצירוף **Much as** פירושו ״אף על פי ש״, לא ״כמו״ ולא ״מפני ש״, והתשובה הנכונה שומרת על יחס הניגוד במילה **Although** (למרות ש).
explanation.en: **Much as** means although, not because, and the correct answer keeps this contrast with **Although** the majority say they care.

items.stem: Nowhere is the city's housing shortage more palpable than in its university district, where rents have nearly doubled in a decade and some students now commute from neighboring towns.
options: The university district is where the city's housing shortage is most keenly felt: rents there have almost doubled in ten years, and some students now travel in from nearby towns.
Nowhere is the city's housing shortage more palpable than in its university district, where rents have more than tripled in a decade and some students now commute from neighboring towns.
The housing shortage weighs more heavily on the university district than on other parts of the city; rents there have nearly doubled in a decade, and most students now come in from surrounding towns.

The university district has done more than the rest of the city to ease the housing shortage, even though some students now commute from neighboring towns and its rents have nearly doubled over the past ten years.

explanation.he: המבנה **Nowhere is ... more palpable than** פירושו ״מורגש ביותר״, והתשובה הנכונה שומרת עליו ועל הפרטים **almost doubled** (כמעט הוכפלו) ו־**some students** (חלק מהסטודנטים).
explanation.en: **Nowhere is ... more palpable than** means most keenly felt, and the correct answer keeps it along with **almost doubled** and **some students**.

items.stem: However ostentatious the canal-side homes of the city's merchants appeared from the street, their interiors were often furnished so plainly that visitors from abroad remarked on the contrast.
options: However ostentatious the canal-side homes of the city's merchants appeared from the street, their interiors were rarely furnished so plainly that visitors from abroad remarked on the contrast.
Long before the city's merchants gave their canal-side homes such showy street fronts, foreign guests had commented on how simply the interiors were furnished.
The city's merchants often furnished their canal-side homes so simply that foreign visitors commented on the contrast with the exteriors, however showy those looked from the street.
Visitors from abroad, however ostentatious their own homes, often remarked that the merchants furnished their canal-side houses too plainly to impress passers-by from the street.

explanation.he: הצירוף **often furnished so plainly** אומר שהריהוט הפשוט היה נפוץ למרות החזית הראוותנית (**However ostentatious**), והתשובה הנכונה שומרת על שניהם במילה **often** ובצירוף **however showy**.
explanation.en: **However ostentatious** the fronts, the interiors were **often furnished so plainly** that visitors noticed, and the correct answer keeps both with **often** and **however showy**.

items.stem: Most of the quotations in one celebrated nineteenth-century dictionary were gathered by zealous unpaid volunteers, whose handwritten slips were then sorted and checked by a small team of salaried editors.
options: Zealous unpaid volunteers, hoping to see their names in print, gathered most of the quotations in one celebrated nineteenth-century dictionary, and a small team of salaried editors then sorted and checked their slips.

Enthusiastic unpaid volunteers collected a few of the quotations in one celebrated nineteenth-century dictionary; their handwritten slips were later sorted and checked by a small team of editors on the payroll.
Most of the quotations gathered by a small team of salaried editors were sorted and checked by zealous unpaid volunteers before appearing in one celebrated nineteenth-century dictionary.
A small team of paid editors sorted and checked the handwritten slips on which eager unpaid volunteers had collected most of the quotations for one celebrated nineteenth-century dictionary.

explanation.he: לפי הצירוף **gathered by zealous unpaid volunteers** המתנדבים אספו את רוב הציטוטים והעורכים רק מיינו ובדקו, והתשובה הנכונה שומרת על החלוקה הזו ועל הכמות (**most**, רוב).
explanation.en: The volunteers **gathered** most quotations and the editors **sorted and checked** them, and the correct answer keeps these roles and **most**.

items.stem: No fewer than four in five of the undergraduates surveyed claimed to have read the assigned novel, yet barely a third of them could give a cogent summary of its plot.
options: No fewer than four in five of the undergraduates surveyed claimed to have read the assigned novel, and most of those students could give a cogent summary of its plot.
At least eighty percent of the undergraduates surveyed said that they had read the assigned novel, but only about a third were able to summarize its plot coherently.
At least four in five of the undergraduates surveyed had actually read the assigned novel, though barely a third of them could sum up its plot clearly.
Barely a third of the undergraduates surveyed claimed to have read the assigned novel, yet more than three-quarters of them could give a cogent summary of its plot.

explanation.he: הצירוף **claimed to have read** (טענו שקראו) והצירוף **barely a third** (בקושי שליש) נשמרים בתשובה הנכונה בצירופים **said that they had read** ו־**only about a third**.
explanation.en: The correct answer keeps **claimed to have read** as **said that they had read** and **barely a third** as **only about a third**.

items.stem: So raucous were the weekend parties in the apartment upstairs that the couple below, having put up with them for over a year, moved out two months before their lease ran out.
options: The couple downstairs put up with the rowdy weekend parties above them for over a year, but the noise drove them out two months before their lease ended.
So raucous were the weekend parties in the apartment upstairs that the couple below moved out within two months, more than a year before their lease ran out.
The weekend parties in the apartment above were so noisy that the couple living downstairs, who had put up with them for over a year, eventually decided to move out.
So raucous were the couple below that the neighbors upstairs, having put up with them for over a year, stopped holding weekend parties two months before their lease ran out.

explanation.he: המבנה **So raucous were the weekend parties ... that** אומר שהרעש הוא שגרם לזוג לעזוב, והתשובה הנכונה שומרת על כך ועל שני הזמנים: **for over a year** ו־**two months before their lease ended**.
explanation.en: **So raucous ... that** makes the noise the cause, and the correct answer keeps both time details: **for over a year** and **two months before their lease ended**.

items.stem: But for the chlorination of drinking water, introduced in many cities early in the twentieth century, waterborne diseases such as typhoid, once rife in crowded neighborhoods, might still kill thousands every year.
options: Despite the chlorination of drinking water, introduced in many cities early in the twentieth century, waterborne diseases such as typhoid, once rife in crowded neighborhoods, still kill thousands every year.
Waterborne diseases such as typhoid were once common in crowded neighborhoods, and many cities began chlorinating their drinking water soon after 1900.

Had many cities not started chlorinating drinking water in the early 1900s, typhoid and other waterborne diseases, formerly widespread in crowded neighborhoods, might still claim thousands of lives a year.
But for the crowded neighborhoods where typhoid was once rife, many cities might not have begun to treat their water supplies with chlorine early in the twentieth century.

explanation.he: הצירוף **But for** פירושו ״אלמלא״, כלומר הכלור הוא שמונע את המוות, והתשובה הנכונה שומרת על כך במבנה **Had many cities not started chlorinating** (אילו ערים רבות לא היו מתחילות להוסיף כלור).
explanation.en: **But for** means without, so chlorination is what prevents the deaths, which the correct answer keeps with **Had many cities not started chlorinating**.

items.stem: In one study, the more dishes a menu listed, the less satisfied diners were with whatever they ordered, perhaps because a surfeit of options made it easier to imagine a better choice.
options: One study found that the longer the menu, the lower diners' satisfaction with their order, perhaps because an excess of options made it easier to picture a better alternative.
In one study, the more dishes a menu listed, the less satisfied diners were with whatever they ordered, since a surfeit of options made it easier for them to imagine a better choice.
According to one study, diners tended to be less pleased with whatever they ordered from longer menus.
In one study, diners who imagined that another dish would have been a better choice ordered more of the dishes on the menu, perhaps because they were less satisfied.

explanation.he: המילה **perhaps** (אולי) מראה שההסבר הוא השערה בלבד, והתשובה הנכונה שומרת עליה וגם על הקשר **the more ... the less** בצירוף **the longer the menu, the lower** (ככל שהתפריט ארוך יותר, כך נמוכה יותר).
explanation.en: **perhaps** marks the explanation as a guess, and the correct answer keeps it along with **the more ... the less** as **the longer the menu, the lower**.

items.stem: Every Saturday, my grandmother goes to the ________ to buy fresh fruit and vegetables.
options: stadium
market
museum
cinema

explanation.he: הסבתא הולכת לקנות פירות וירקות טריים (**to buy fresh fruit and vegetables**), ולכן התשובה היא **market** (שוק).
explanation.en: She goes there **to buy fresh fruit and vegetables**, and a **market** is where people buy them.

items.stem: The soup was too ________ to eat, so we waited a few minutes for it to cool down.
options: salty
spicy
hot
tasty

explanation.he: המילה **so** (לכן) מצביעה על תוצאה: חיכינו שהמרק יתקרר (**for it to cool down**), ולכן הוא היה חם מדי: **hot** (חם).
explanation.en: The word **so** shows a result: we waited **for it to cool down**, so the soup was too **hot**.

items.stem: My shoes are very ________ – there is mud all over them.
options: loud
lucky
old
dirty

explanation.he: ההסבר שאחרי המקף, **there is mud all over them** (יש עליהן בוץ בכל מקום), מתאר נעליים לא נקיות, ולכן התשובה היא **dirty** (מלוכלך).
explanation.en: The explanation after the dash, **there is mud all over them**, describes shoes that are **dirty**.

items.stem: When the teacher came in, we all stood up and ________ good morning.
options: said
spoke
talked
showed

explanation.he: עם הברכה **good morning** (בוקר טוב) משתמשים בפועל **say**, ולכן צורת העבר הנכונה היא **said** (אמרנו).
explanation.en: We **say** **good morning**, so the correct past form here is **said**.

items.stem: The road was icy, so the drivers went very ________ to stay safe.
options: loudly
happily
carelessly
slowly

explanation.he: המילה **so** (לכן) מראה תוצאה של כביש קפוא (**The road was icy**), והמטרה **to stay safe** (להישאר בטוחים) מחייבת זהירות, ולכן הנהגים נסעו **slowly** (לאט).
explanation.en: The word **so** shows a result of the **icy** road, and **to stay safe** means being careful, so the drivers went **slowly**.

items.stem: Our school sells healthy ________, such as apples, carrots and nuts.
options: snacks
drinks
tickets
toys

explanation.he: הצירוף **such as** (כמו) מציג דוגמאות: תפוחים, גזר ואגוזים (**apples, carrots and nuts**) הם אוכל קטן ובריא, ולכן התשובה היא **snacks** (נשנושים).
explanation.en: The examples after **such as**, **apples, carrots and nuts**, are small foods people eat between meals, so the answer is **snacks**.

items.stem: If you do not understand the lesson, please raise your hand and ________ a question.
options: say
ask
answer
send

explanation.he: עם שם העצם **question** (שאלה) באנגלית משתמשים בפועל **ask**, ולכן התשובה היא **ask** (לשאול).
explanation.en: The noun **question** goes with the verb **ask**, and a student who does not understand wants to ask.

items.stem: My aunt is very ________ – she shares her lunch with everyone and gives clothes to people in need.
options: angry
shy
kind
busy

explanation.he: ההסבר שאחרי המקף (**shares her lunch with everyone and gives clothes**) מתאר אישה שאוהבת לעזור, ולכן התשובה היא **kind** (טובת לב).
explanation.en: The explanation after the dash, **shares her lunch with everyone and gives clothes**, describes someone who cares about others, so she is **kind**.

items.stem: Although the film had a famous director and a huge budget, most critics found it ________.
options: dull
remarkable
exciting
relaxing

explanation.he: המילה **Although** (למרות ש) מסמנת ניגוד לבמאי המפורסם ולתקציב הענק (**a famous director and a huge budget**), ולכן המבקרים מצאו את הסרט **dull** (משעמם).
explanation.en: The word **Although** signals a contrast with **a famous director and a huge budget**, so the critics found the film **dull**.

items.stem: Our village is slowly ________: every year more young people leave for the cities, and fewer children are born.
options: expanding
spreading
shrinking
improving

explanation.he: ההסבר שאחרי הנקודתיים (**more young people leave for the cities, and fewer children are born**) מתאר יישוב שאוכלוסייתו הולכת וקטנה, ולכן התשובה היא **shrinking** (הולך וקטן).
explanation.en: The explanation after the colon, **more young people leave for the cities, and fewer children are born**, describes a village that is getting smaller, so it is **shrinking**.

items.stem: Farmers in this part of the country grow many different kinds of ________, for example wheat, corn and rice.
options: animals
seasons
buildings
crops

explanation.he: הצירוף **for example** (למשל) מציג דוגמאות: חיטה, תירס ואורז (**wheat, corn and rice**) הם צמחים שחקלאים מגדלים, ולכן התשובה היא **crops** (גידולים, יבולים).
explanation.en: The examples after **for example**, **wheat, corn and rice**, are plants that farmers grow, so the answer is **crops**.

items.stem: After years of hard work and saving money, Lina's dream of opening her own shop finally ________ true.
options: went
came
grew
rose

explanation.he: עם המילה **true** (אמיתי) באנגלית אומרים **come true** (להתגשם), ולכן צורת העבר הנכונה היא **came** (התגשם).
explanation.en: The phrase **come true** means that a dream becomes real, so the past form here is **came**.

items.stem: The instructions were so confusing that many students ________ the question, and they wrote about a different topic.
options: copied
translated
underlined
misread

explanation.he: התחילית **mis-** פירושה בטעות, ולכן המילה **misread** (קראו לא נכון) מסבירה למה התלמידים כתבו על נושא אחר (**wrote about a different topic**).
explanation.en: The prefix **mis-** means wrongly, so **misread** explains why the students **wrote about a different topic**.

items.stem: Because the problem was serious, the managers called a meeting to ________ it before making any decision.
options: discuss
speak
complain
talk

explanation.he: בגלל בעיה חמורה (**the problem was serious**) קוראים לפגישה כדי לדון בה, והפועל **discuss** (לדון) בא ישירות לפני הכינוי **it**, ולכן הוא התשובה.
explanation.en: Because **the problem was serious**, the managers met to **discuss** it, and only **discuss** takes **it** directly.

items.stem: Since the restaurant has only a few tables, it is wise to ________ a table early if you want to eat there on Saturday.
options: order
cook
book
taste

explanation.he: המילה **Since** (מכיוון ש) מסבירה שיש מעט שולחנות (**only a few tables**), ולכן כדאי להזמין שולחן מראש: **book** (להזמין).
explanation.en: The word **Since** gives the reason: there are **only a few tables**, so it is wise to **book** one early.

items.stem: Although the symptoms of the illness are dramatic in its late stages, its earliest signs are so ________ that even experienced doctors often miss them.
options: alarming
obvious
painful
subtle

explanation.he: המילה **Although** מעמידה את הסימפטומים הדרמטיים של השלב המאוחר (**dramatic in its late stages**) מול הסימנים המוקדמים, שרופאים מנוסים מחמיצים (**often miss them**), ולכן התשובה היא **subtle** (עדין, קשה להבחנה).
explanation.en: **Although** contrasts the **dramatic** late symptoms with the earliest signs, which doctors **often miss**, so the answer is **subtle** (hard to notice).

items.stem: Fresh-flower sellers may earn a large profit on Monday, but the market is notoriously ________: prices change so quickly that by Friday the same stock may be sold at a loss.
options: profitable
overpriced
erratic
conventional

explanation.he: הנקודתיים מסבירים שהמחירים משתנים במהירות (**prices change so quickly**) ועלולים להפוך רווח להפסד, ולכן השוק הוא **erratic** (לא יציב, חסר סדר).
explanation.en: **But** contrasts Monday's profit with a possible loss, and **prices change so quickly** shows the market is **erratic** (irregular, without a pattern).

items.stem: Although most ancient cities grew up beside rivers, a few developed in ________ places, such as mountain passes, desert oases and tiny offshore islands.
options: fertile
remote
coastal
northern

explanation.he: הצירוף **such as** מביא דוגמאות (**mountain passes, desert oases and tiny offshore islands**), וכולן מקומות רחוקים וקשים להגעה, ולכן התשובה היא **remote** (מרוחק, נידח).
explanation.en: **Such as** gives examples (**mountain passes, desert oases and tiny offshore islands**), all far from other places, so the answer is **remote** (far away).

items.stem: Although the new bridge was built to ________ congestion in the old town, drivers soon found that their journeys took longer than before.
options: ease
worsen
monitor
record

explanation.he: המילה **Although** מעמידה את מטרת הבנייה (**was built to**) מול התוצאה הגרועה (**took longer than before**), ולכן המטרה הייתה **ease** (להקל על, להפחית).
explanation.en: **Although** contrasts the purpose (**was built to**) with the bad result (**took longer than before**), so the aim was to **ease** (make less severe) the congestion.

items.stem: Most people believe that they are better drivers than average; yet this cannot be true for everyone, because people consistently ________ their own skills.
options: underestimate
develop
measure
overestimate

explanation.he: המילה **yet** מראה שהאמונה של רוב האנשים שהם עצמם נהגים טובים מהממוצע (**better drivers than average**) אינה יכולה להיות נכונה לכולם, ולכן התשובה היא **overestimate** (להעריך יתר על המידה).
explanation.en: **Yet** says the belief in being **better drivers than average** cannot be true for everyone, so people **overestimate** (judge too highly) their skills.

items.stem: While several small shops on the main street closed during the recession, the staid old bookshop managed to ________ the storm by cutting costs and selling rare editions online.
options: cause
weather
predict
enjoy

explanation.he: המילה **While** מעמידה את החנויות שנסגרו (**closed during the recession**) מול החנות ששרדה, והצירוף הקבוע **weather the storm** פירושו לצלוח תקופה קשה (לשרוד).
explanation.en: **While** contrasts the shops that **closed during the recession** with one that survived, and the phrase **weather the storm** means to get through hard times.

items.stem: Even though the new filter was designed to block every unsuitable website, curious teenagers soon found simple ways to ________ it.
options: circumvent
implement
upgrade
demonstrate

explanation.he: הצירוף **Even though** מעמיד את מטרת המסנן (**designed to block every unsuitable website**) מול הנערים שמצאו דרכים פשוטות להתחמק ממנו, ולכן התשובה היא **circumvent** (לעקוף).
explanation.en: **Even though** sets the filter's aim (**designed to block every unsuitable website**) against teenagers who found simple ways to **circumvent** (get around) it.

items.stem: The island's famous seabirds appear to thrive; nevertheless, a recent census shows that their numbers are quietly ________: each year, fewer chicks hatch than in the year before.
options: multiplying
recovering
diminishing
evolving

explanation.he: הנקודתיים מסבירים שבכל שנה בוקעים פחות גוזלים (**fewer chicks hatch than in the year before**), והמילה **nevertheless** מעמידה זאת מול המראה המשגשג, ולכן התשובה היא **diminishing** (הולך וקטן).
explanation.en: **Nevertheless** contrasts the thriving look with the colon's explanation, **fewer chicks hatch than in the year before**, so the numbers are **diminishing** (getting smaller).

items.stem: Whereas primary-school pupils usually learn best through play, university students tend to prefer ________ teaching, with clear definitions and worked examples.
options: playful
outdoor
structured
continuous

explanation.he: המילה **Whereas** מעמידה למידה דרך משחק (**through play**) מול העדפת הסטודנטים, והפרטים **clear definitions and worked examples** מתארים הוראה **structured** (מובנית, מסודרת).
explanation.en: **Whereas** contrasts learning **through play** with the students' preference, and **clear definitions and worked examples** describe **structured** (carefully organized) teaching.

items.stem: In spite of the council's insistence that its new parking rules are ________, applying the same charges to residents and visitors alike, many shop owners say that the rules harm those who live nearby.
options: selective
ambitious
costly
equitable

explanation.he: הצירוף **applying the same charges to residents and visitors alike** מגדיר את החסר: כללים שמתייחסים לכולם באותה צורה הם **equitable** (הוגנים), למרות הטענה של בעלי החנויות.
explanation.en: The phrase **applying the same charges to residents and visitors alike** defines the blank: rules that treat everyone the same are **equitable** (fair).

items.stem: Although some metals, such as iron and steel, rust easily in damp air, others, such as gold and platinum, are highly ________, which is why they stay bright for thousands of years.
options: unreactive
reactive
widespread
precious

explanation.he: המילה **Although** מעמידה מתכות שמחלידות (**rust easily in damp air**) מול הזהב והפלטינה, שנשארים נוצצים (**stay bright for thousands of years**), ולכן הם **unreactive** (שאינם מגיבים בקלות).
explanation.en: **Although** contrasts metals that **rust easily in damp air** with gold and platinum, which **stay bright for thousands of years** because they are **unreactive** (do not react easily).

items.stem: Although the actor ________ great pains to appear relaxed in interviews, his friends say that he rehearses every answer in advance.
options: makes
takes
gives
holds

explanation.he: הצירוף הקבוע **take great pains to** פירושו להשקיע מאמץ רב כדי שדבר יצליח, וזה מתאים לשחקן שמתאמן על כל תשובה (**rehearses every answer in advance**), ולכן התשובה היא **takes**.
explanation.en: The fixed phrase **take great pains to** means to make a great effort, which fits an actor who **rehearses every answer in advance**, so the answer is **takes**.

items.stem: Although the poem seems at first to be an artless love song, its final stanza gives the whole text a ________ meaning, suggesting that the speaker is in fact mourning a lost childhood.
options: romantic
profound
literal
comic

explanation.he: המילה **Although** מעמידה את הקריאה הראשונה (**seems at first to be an artless love song**) מול הבית האחרון, שמגלה התאבלות על ילדות אבודה (**mourning a lost childhood**), ולכן המשמעות היא **profound** (עמוקה).
explanation.en: **Although** contrasts the simple first reading with the final stanza's **mourning a lost childhood**, so the meaning is **profound** (deep and serious).

items.stem: Because the faint signal had been recorded by a single instrument, the astronomers called their detection of methane on the torrid planet ________, promising a firmer verdict once a second observatory had checked the data.
options: tentative
definitive
inadvertent
groundbreaking

explanation.he: אות חלש שנקלט במכשיר אחד בלבד (**recorded by a single instrument**) והבטחה להכרעה מוצקה יותר בהמשך (**promising a firmer verdict**) מראים שהממצא עוד לא סופי, ולכן התשובה היא **tentative** (ראשוני, לא סופי).
explanation.en: A faint signal **recorded by a single instrument** and **promising a firmer verdict** show the finding is not yet final, so it is **tentative** (provisional).

items.stem: Stripped of tone of voice and facial expression, short text messages are easily ________: a single 'fine' from even the most phlegmatic colleague may read as cold annoyance or as cheerful agreement.
options: mistyped
overstated
misaddressed
misconstrued

explanation.he: בלי טון דיבור ובלי הבעת פנים (**Stripped of tone of voice and facial expression**) אותה מילה יכולה להתפרש כרוגז או כהסכמה, ולכן התשובה היא **misconstrued** (מתפרש באופן שגוי).
explanation.en: **Stripped of tone of voice and facial expression**, one word **may read as cold annoyance or as cheerful agreement**, so messages are **misconstrued** (misunderstood).

items.stem: Whereas the old bus service had been notoriously ________, arriving early one day and forty minutes late the next, the new one keeps so closely to its timetable that commuters set their watches by it.
options: sluggish
fitful
overcrowded
dilatory

explanation.he: המילה **Whereas** מנגידה את השירות הישן לשירות חדש שמדייק בזמנים, והתיאור **arriving early one day and forty minutes late the next** מראה חוסר סדירות, ולכן התשובה היא **fitful** (לא סדיר, מקוטע).
explanation.en: **Whereas** contrasts the old service with a punctual one, and **arriving early one day and forty minutes late the next** shows irregularity, so it was **fitful**.

items.stem: Even though the pines planted on the parched hillsides were meant to ________ soil erosion, their dense shade killed the grasses whose roots held the soil, and the slopes washed away faster.
options: aggravate
mediate
mitigate
irrigate

explanation.he: המילים **Even though** ו**were meant to** מראות שהכוונה הייתה הפוכה לתוצאה, מדרונות שנסחפו מהר יותר (**the slopes washed away faster**), ולכן התשובה היא **mitigate** (למתן, להפחית).
explanation.en: **Even though** and **were meant to** show the aim was the opposite of the result, **the slopes washed away faster**, so the answer is **mitigate** (reduce).

items.stem: The writing instructor gave every class the same advice: be ________, saying in ten words what others say in fifty, yet never cutting a fact that the reader actually needs.
options: lucid
prolix
succinct
evocative

explanation.he: לומר בעשר מילים מה שאחרים אומרים בחמישים (**saying in ten words what others say in fifty**) בלי להשמיט עובדה נחוצה פירושו להיות **succinct** (תמציתי).
explanation.en: **Saying in ten words what others say in fifty** without **cutting a fact that the reader actually needs** means being **succinct** (brief but complete).

items.stem: The engineer never particularly enjoyed studying languages, yet she had a remarkable ________ for them: posted abroad, she could hold simple conversations in each new language within weeks.
options: reverence
predilection
aversion
aptitude

explanation.he: המילה **yet** מנגידה את החסר להנאה שלא הייתה, וההסבר **she could hold simple conversations in each new language within weeks** מתאר יכולת, ולכן התשובה היא **aptitude** (כישרון טבעי).
explanation.en: **Yet** contrasts the blank with enjoyment, and **she could hold simple conversations in each new language within weeks** shows ability, so it is **aptitude** (talent).

items.stem: As any sagacious investor knows, many of a firm's most valuable assets are ________ ones, such as its brand's reputation, its patents and its customers' loyalty, none of which can be stacked in a warehouse.
options: intangible
liquid
tangential
fixed

explanation.he: הדוגמאות **its brand's reputation, its patents and its customers' loyalty** והצירוף **none of which can be stacked in a warehouse** מתארים נכסים בלי צורה פיזית, ולכן התשובה היא **intangible** (בלתי מוחשי).
explanation.en: The examples, **its brand's reputation, its patents and its customers' loyalty**, cannot **be stacked in a warehouse**, so they are **intangible** (non-physical) assets.

items.stem: Some of the most ________ animals, such as the octopus, which uses its sinuous arms to unscrew jars of shrimp, and the crow, which bends wire into hooks, solve problems their ancestors never faced.
options: industrious
ingenious
predatory
ingenuous

explanation.he: הדוגמאות, תמנון שפותח צנצנות ועורב שמכופף חוט לצורת וו, וההמשך **solve problems their ancestors never faced** מתארים כושר המצאה, ולכן התשובה היא **ingenious** (מחוכם, בעל כושר המצאה).
explanation.en: Unscrewing jars, bending **wire into hooks** and solving **problems their ancestors never faced** show inventiveness, so the animals are **ingenious** (clever and inventive).

items.stem: Many firms pay lip ________ to work-life balance: their glossy brochures extol it at length, yet managers still expect staff to answer emails at midnight.
options: service
tribute
heed
attention

explanation.he: הצירוף הקבוע **pay lip service to** (לתת מס שפתיים) מתאים לשבחים (**extol it at length**) שאין מאחוריהם מעשים (**answer emails at midnight**), ולכן התשובה היא **service**.
explanation.en: The fixed phrase **pay lip service to** (praise without action) fits brochures that **extol it at length** while managers still expect staff to **answer emails at midnight**.

items.stem: Today's placid fishing village, where a few boats drift in at dusk, is a far ________ from the bustling port that, three centuries ago, shipped grain and timber across the Baltic Sea.
options: call
breadth
shout
cry

explanation.he: הצירוף הקבוע **a far cry from** (שונה לגמרי מ...) מתאים לניגוד בין כפר דייגים שקט לבין הנמל ההומה (**the bustling port**) של פעם, ולכן התשובה היא **cry**.
explanation.en: The fixed phrase **a far cry from** (very different from) fits the contrast between a quiet village and **the bustling port** it once was, so the answer is **cry**.

items.stem: Decades in a damp basement caused ________ damage to the letters of a loquacious nineteenth-century composer: the ink faded and the paper crumbled, so that whole pages can never be read again.
options: superficial
illegible
irreparable
indefensible

explanation.he: נזק שבגללו דפים שלמים לא ייקראו לעולם (**whole pages can never be read again**) הוא נזק שאי אפשר לתקן, ולכן התשובה היא **irreparable** (**ir-** + **repair** + **-able**: שאין לו תקנה).
explanation.en: Damage after which **whole pages can never be read again** cannot be repaired, so it is **irreparable** (ir- + repair + -able).

items.stem: With the benefit of ________, many investors insist that they saw the market crash coming, yet remarkably few of these voluble forecasters sold their own shares beforehand.
options: foresight
hindsight
insight
oversight

explanation.he: המשקיעים טוענים רק עכשיו שראו את הקריסה מראש, אבל מעטים מהם מכרו מניות לפני כן (**sold their own shares beforehand**), ולכן התשובה היא **hindsight** (חוכמה בדיעבד).
explanation.en: They **insist** now that they **saw the market crash coming**, yet few **sold their own shares beforehand**, so this is **hindsight** (wisdom after the event).

items.stem: The success of the vaccination campaign in remote villages ________ on keeping the doses cold: a single afternoon in a stalled, unrefrigerated truck on the serpentine mountain roads could spoil an entire shipment.
options: insisted
hinged
dwelt
embarked

explanation.he: הנושא **The success of the vaccination campaign** אינו יכול להתעקש או להרהר, וההסבר שאחרי הנקודתיים מראה תלות מוחלטת בקירור, ולכן התשובה היא **hinged** (**hinge on**: להיות תלוי ב...).
explanation.en: A **success** cannot insist or dwell, and the colon shows total dependence on cold doses, so the answer is **hinged** (**hinge on** = depend on).

items.stem: After years of quarrels, the two cantankerous founders split their company, and each went back to his ________ field: one to designing batteries, the other to writing software.
options: respectful
prospective
respective
introspective

explanation.he: הצירוף **each went back to his** וההסבר **one to designing batteries, the other to writing software** מראים שכל אחד חזר לתחום שלו, ולכן התשובה היא **respective** (של כל אחד בנפרד).
explanation.en: **Each went back to his** own field, **one to designing batteries, the other to writing software**, so the answer is **respective** (belonging to each one separately).

items.stem: Seldom has so famously ________ a critic written so glowing a review: she called the young novelist's debut the most assured first book she had read in a decade.
options: effusive
charitable
urbane
acerbic

explanation.he: המילה **Seldom** (לעיתים רחוקות) מראה שביקורת נלהבת כל כך (**so glowing a review**) היא חריגה אצל המבקרת הזאת, ולכן התשובה היא **acerbic** (חריפה ועוקצנית).
explanation.en: **Seldom** marks a review this **glowing** as unusual for her, so she must be known for biting criticism: **acerbic** (sharply critical).

items.stem: Far from being a late cultural acquisition, a sense of fairness seems ________ in toddlers, who already protest petulantly when a playmate gets more treats, though not yet when they themselves do.
options: incipient
latent
full-blown
atrophied

explanation.he: הפעוטות כבר מוחים (**already protest**) כשחבר מקבל יותר, אבל עדיין לא כשהם עצמם מקבלים יותר (**though not yet**), ולכן החוש קיים רק בתחילתו: **incipient** (מתהווה, ראשוני).
explanation.en: Toddlers **already protest** but **not yet** in every case, so their sense of fairness has begun yet is incomplete: **incipient** (just starting to develop).

items.stem: Wary of buying looted antiquities, museums now scrutinize the ________ of every object they acquire, for example by tracing a statue back through each dealer and collector who has owned it.
options: appraisal
patrimony
provenance
iconography

explanation.he: הדוגמה מתארת מעקב אחר כל סוחר ואספן שהחזיקו בפסל (**tracing a statue back through each dealer and collector**), ולכן התשובה היא **provenance** (מקור ותולדות הבעלות של חפץ).
explanation.en: The example, **tracing a statue back through each dealer and collector**, describes an object's ownership history: its **provenance** (origin and chain of owners).

items.stem: Professional reviews of the new phone run the ________ from rapturous to withering, which leaves shoppers, already faced with a bewildering profusion of rival models, little the wiser.
options: course
gamut
gauntlet
errand

explanation.he: הצירוף **from rapturous to withering** מתאר טווח שלם מקצה לקצה, והצירוף הקבוע **run the gamut from** פירושו לכסות את כל הקשת, ולכן התשובה היא **gamut** (כל הטווח, מכלול).
explanation.en: The range **from rapturous to withering** calls for the fixed phrase **run the gamut**, meaning to cover every point between two extremes: **gamut**.

items.stem: Her years as a waitress in a busy diner stood her in good ________ when she later took over a down-at-heel hotel and had to keep both guests and staff content.
options: stead
standing
shape
faith

explanation.he: המילים **stood her in good** פותחות את הצירוף הקבוע **stand someone in good stead** (להועיל למישהו בהמשך הדרך), ולכן התשובה היא **stead**.
explanation.en: The words **stood her in good** begin the fixed phrase **stand someone in good stead**, meaning to prove useful later: **stead**.

items.stem: Rather than state plainly that the pilot program had failed, the agency's report resorted to ________, spending three long paragraphs edging around a fact that four words could have conveyed.
options: eloquence
circumlocution
circumspection
soliloquy

explanation.he: הדוח השתמש בשלוש פסקאות ארוכות כדי לעקוף עובדה (**edging around a fact**) במקום לומר אותה ישירות (**state plainly**), ולכן התשובה היא **circumlocution** (דיבור עקיף ומסורבל, 'סחור סחור').
explanation.en: Instead of saying it **plainly**, the report spent **three long paragraphs edging around a fact**, which is **circumlocution** (roundabout, wordy speech).

items.stem: She received the university's acceptance letter and, a week later, its rejection of her scholarship application with the same ________, neither celebrating the one nor lamenting the other.
options: animosity
animation
equanimity
magnanimity

explanation.he: המילים **neither celebrating the one nor lamenting the other** מתארות רוח שקולה זהה מול בשורה טובה ובשורה רעה, ולכן התשובה היא **equanimity** (שלוות נפש, יישוב דעת).
explanation.en: The phrase **neither celebrating the one nor lamenting the other** describes the same calm mind in good and bad news alike: **equanimity** (calm composure).

items.stem: Rather than reject the union's increasingly strident demands outright, management chose to ________, promising a review here and a working group there in the hope that the issue would quietly fade.
options: capitulate
dither
retaliate
temporize

explanation.he: ההנהלה פיזרה הבטחות כדי שהעניין ייעלם מעצמו (**in the hope that the issue would quietly fade**), כלומר משכה זמן בכוונה, ולכן התשובה היא **temporize** (להרוויח זמן, לדחות הכרעה).
explanation.en: Management made vague promises **in the hope that the issue would quietly fade**, deliberately stalling: **temporize** (delay to gain time).

items.stem: Although the mountain stream looks perfectly clear, its water is far from ________: laboratory tests routinely find parasites that can cause severe stomach illness in hikers who drink it untreated.
options: pellucid
tepid
potable
brackish

explanation.he: המים נראים צלולים, אבל בבדיקות מוצאים בהם טפילים שגורמים למחלה אצל מי ששותה אותם (**hikers who drink it untreated**), ולכן התשובה היא **potable** (ראוי לשתייה).
explanation.en: Tests find parasites that sicken **hikers who drink it untreated**, so the clear-looking water is unsafe to drink: far from **potable** (drinkable).

items.stem: Before astronomers could predict their orbits, comets were widely regarded as ________ omens: their sudden appearance was taken to foretell floods, failed harvests or the fall of rulers.
options: benign
baleful
fictitious
trivial

explanation.he: לפי ההסבר שאחרי הנקודתיים, הופעת השביטים נחשבה לסימן לשיטפונות, ליבול כושל ולנפילת שליטים (**to foretell floods, failed harvests or the fall of rulers**), ולכן התשובה היא **baleful** (מבשר רעות, מאיים).
explanation.en: Comets were thought **to foretell floods, failed harvests or the fall of rulers**, so they were threatening signs: **baleful** (menacing, harmful).

items.stem: Instead of hosting the genteel debate their founders imagined, many online comment sections turn ________ within a dozen replies, as polite disagreement over a recipe gives way to personal insults.
options: vitriolic
frivolous
rambling
insipid

explanation.he: אי-הסכמה מנומסת הופכת לעלבונות אישיים (**gives way to personal insults**), כלומר הטון נעשה ארסי ועוין, ולכן התשובה היא **vitriolic** (ארסי, מלא שנאה).
explanation.en: Polite disagreement **gives way to personal insults**, so the comments turn bitterly hostile: **vitriolic** (full of venom).

items.stem: Some invasive plants owe their conquest of riverbanks less to hardiness than to sheer ________: a single nondescript weed, for example, can shed tens of thousands of seeds in a season.
options: longevity
resilience
sterility
fecundity

explanation.he: הדוגמה מתארת עשב אחד שמפיל עשרות אלפי זרעים בעונה (**can shed tens of thousands of seeds in a season**), ולכן סוד ההצלחה הוא ריבוי עצום, והתשובה היא **fecundity** (פוריות).
explanation.en: The example, a weed that **can shed tens of thousands of seeds in a season**, shows sheer reproductive power: **fecundity** (fertility).

items.stem: Critics dismissed the newly created post of heritage adviser as a ________: it carried a generous salary and ample perquisites, yet demanded little beyond the occasional ribbon-cutting.
options: sinecure
pittance
vocation
stopgap

explanation.he: המשרה מעניקה משכורת נדיבה והטבות (**a generous salary and ample perquisites**) אך כמעט אינה דורשת עבודה (**demanded little**), ולכן התשובה היא **sinecure** (משרה נוחה ומכניסה בלי עבודה של ממש).
explanation.en: The post offers **a generous salary and ample perquisites** yet **demanded little**, so it is a **sinecure** (a well-paid job with almost no work).

items.stem: Although the octogenarian diplomat's memoir is riddled with errors of date and name, it would be unfair to call it ________: its author never invents an episode but merely misremembers a few.
options: erroneous
disjointed
unoriginal
mendacious

explanation.he: המחבר אינו ממציא אף אירוע אלא רק טועה בזיכרונו (**never invents an episode but merely misremembers a few**), ולכן אי אפשר להאשים אותו בשקר, והתשובה היא **mendacious** (שקרי, כוזב במכוון).
explanation.en: The author **never invents an episode but merely misremembers a few**, so the memoir is mistaken, not lying, and it is unfair to call it **mendacious** (deliberately untruthful).

items.sentence: We need ten more ________ and forks, because our guests are coming for dinner tonight.

explanation.he: המילה **ten** והצירוף **and forks** מראים שצריך שם עצם ברבים, וברבים של שם העצם **knife** האות **f** מתחלפת באות **v**, ולכן התשובה היא **knives** (סכינים).
explanation.en: The word **ten** and the phrase **and forks** call for a plural noun, and **knife** changes **f** to **v**: **knives**.

items.sentence: Last October the birds ________ south to warmer countries, and they came back in the spring.

explanation.he: הצירוף **Last October** והפועל **came back** מראים שצריך פועל בעבר, והפועל **fly** חריג, ולכן התשובה היא **flew** (עפו).
explanation.en: The phrase **Last October** and the verb **came back** call for the past simple, and **fly** is irregular: **flew**.

items.sentence: Because Dan was ________ as captain by all the other players, he will lead the team in Saturday's game.

explanation.he: בין הצירוף **Dan was** לבין הצירוף **by all the other players** צריך בינוני סביל, והפועל **choose** חריג, ולכן התשובה היא **chosen** (נבחר).
explanation.en: Between **Dan was** and **by all the other players** we need a passive participle, and **choose** is irregular: **chosen**.

items.sentence: Although the concert was wonderful, we sat ________ on hard wooden benches for three hours, so our backs hurt afterward.

explanation.he: אחרי הפועל **sat** צריך תואר פועל, והצירוף **our backs hurt** מחייב שלילה, ולכן התשובה היא **uncomfortably** (בחוסר נוחות).
explanation.en: After **sat** we need an adverb, and **our backs hurt** makes it negative: **uncomfortably**.

items.sentence: The ________ of the old tunnel is only three meters, so tall trucks must use another road.

explanation.he: בין המילה **The** למילה **of** צריך שם עצם, והצירוף **only three meters** מתאר מידה, ולכן התשובה היא **height** (גובה), עם האותיות **ei** והאות **t** בסוף.
explanation.en: Between **The** and **of** we need a noun, and **only three meters** is a measurement: **height**.

items.sentence: ________ meals for the whole week helps many families save money, because they waste less food.

explanation.he: המקום הריק פותח את המשפט ומשמש נושא של הפועל **helps**, ולכן צריך שם פעולה בסיומת **-ing**, עם האות **n** כפולה ועם אות גדולה, כלומר הצורה **Planning** (תכנון).
explanation.en: The blank opens the sentence as the subject of **helps**, so we need an **-ing** form with a double **n** and a capital: **Planning**.

items.sentence: The rocket was ready on time, yet ________ about the weather delayed the launch, since forecasters could not say whether storms would arrive.

explanation.he: לפני הפועל **delayed** חסר נושא, כלומר שם עצם, והחלק **forecasters could not say** מחייב שלילה, ולכן התשובה היא **uncertainty** (חוסר ודאות).
explanation.en: The subject of **delayed** must be a noun, and **forecasters could not say** makes it negative: **uncertainty**.

items.sentence: Even though the old family bank had survived several ________ during its long history, the last one forced it to close for good.

explanation.he: המילה **several** מחייבת שם עצם ברבים, וברבים הסיומת **-is** של שם העצם **crisis** מתחלפת בסיומת **-es**, ולכן התשובה היא **crises** (משברים).
explanation.en: The word **several** needs a plural noun, and **crisis** changes **-is** to **-es**: **crises**.

items.sentence: Many teachers make the ________ that quiet students are shy, whereas often they are simply thinking carefully before they speak.

explanation.he: אחרי הצירוף **make the** צריך שם עצם, והמילה **whereas** מראה שמדובר בהנחה לא מבוססת, ולכן התשובה היא **assumption** (הנחה), עם האות **p** לפני הסיומת **-tion**.
explanation.en: After **make the** we need a noun, and **whereas** shows an untested belief: **assumption**, with a **p** before **-tion**.

items.sentence: Despite having only one week, even the most slothful medical students managed to ________ the names of all 206 bones in the human body.

explanation.he: אחרי הצירוף **managed to** צריך פועל בצורת הבסיס, ומשם העצם **memory** יוצרים את הפועל **memorize** (לשנן, ללמוד בעל-פה), כשהאות **y** נשמטת לפני הסיומת **-ize**.
explanation.en: After **managed to** we need a base-form verb, so **memory** drops its **y** and adds **-ize**: **memorize**.

items.sentence: Although her manager was annoyed about the missed deadline, he was very ________ when she explained that her train had been stuck for two hours.

explanation.he: אחרי הצירוף **he was very** צריך שם תואר שמתאר את המנהל, והמילה **Although** מראה שלמרות הכעס הוא גילה הבנה, ולכן התשובה היא **understanding** (מבין, סבלני).
explanation.en: After **he was very** we need an adjective for a sympathetic person, as **Although** shows: **understanding**, not **understandable**.

items.sentence: Under a deal struck after years of tortuous negotiations, hikers may now cross the private estate without ________ from its owners, provided they keep to the marked trail.

explanation.he: אחרי מילת היחס **without** ולפני הצירוף **from its owners** צריך שם עצם, ולכן מהפועל **hinder** בונים את שם העצם **hindrance** (הפרעה, מכשול), שבו נשמטת האות **e**.
explanation.en: After **without** and before **from its owners** we need a noun, so **hinder** drops its **e** and takes **-ance**: **hindrance**.

items.sentence: Pending a review of the judges' scores, the prize money was ________ from the winning robotics team for a month, prompting querulous emails from its captain.

explanation.he: אחרי הצירוף **the prize money was** צריך צורת סביל, כי מישהו עיכב את הכסף, ולכן הפועל **withhold** הופך לצורה **withheld** (עוכב, לא נמסר).
explanation.en: After **the prize money was** we need a passive participle, because someone held the money back: **withheld**.

items.sentence: Unlike the optional lectures, the Monday safety briefing is ________ for all first-year chemistry students: a dour lab manager turns away anyone who has skipped it.

explanation.he: הצירוף **Unlike the optional lectures** מראה שהתדריך אינו רשות אלא חובה, ולכן אחרי המילה **is** צריך את שם התואר **compulsory** (חובה, מחייב).
explanation.en: **Unlike the optional lectures** shows the briefing is required, so after **is** we need **compulsory**.

items.sentence: Once a quiet fishing village, the island drew tourists in ________ numbers last summer, more than in any earlier year, after a doyen of travel writing praised it.

explanation.he: לפני שם העצם **numbers** צריך שם תואר, והצירוף **more than in any earlier year** מראה שדבר כזה לא קרה מעולם, ולכן התשובה היא **unprecedented** (חסר תקדים).
explanation.en: Before **numbers** we need an adjective, and **more than in any earlier year** means it never happened before: **unprecedented**.

items.sentence: ________, the cloudburst ended minutes before the outdoor wedding began, and guests who had arrived crestfallen under dripping umbrellas enjoyed sunshine until dusk.

explanation.he: בתחילת המשפט ולפני פסיק צריך תואר פועל באות גדולה, והצירוף **enjoyed sunshine until dusk** מראה הקלה, ולכן התשובה היא **Mercifully** (למרבה המזל, למרבה ההקלה).
explanation.en: An adverb opens the sentence, and **enjoyed sunshine until dusk** signals relief: **Mercifully**, with a capital **M**.

items.sentence: More than two hundred ________ of the village school, men and women who had graduated over seven decades, gathered last spring for a reunion hosted by its genial principal.

explanation.he: המספר **More than two hundred** מחייב רבים, והצירוף **men and women** מראה קבוצה מעורבת, ולכן מהיחיד **alumnus** בונים את צורת הרבים **alumni** (בוגרים).
explanation.en: **More than two hundred** needs a plural, and **men and women** rules out the women-only form: **alumni**.

items.sentence: Out of ________ to local custom, even the delegation's famously haughty leader removed his shoes before entering the elderly weaver's home, though nobody had asked him to.

explanation.he: בין הצירוף **Out of** לבין הצירוף **to local custom** צריך שם עצם שמשמעו כבוד מרצון, ולכן התשובה היא **deference** (כבוד, התחשבות), ולא שם עצם של דחייה.
explanation.en: Between **Out of** and **to local custom** we need a noun meaning respect: **deference**, not **deferral** (delay).

items.sentence: Rather than airing their ________ in public, the nurses handed the board's supercilious chair a formal list of them: chronic understaffing, unpaid overtime and outdated equipment.

explanation.he: אחרי הצירוף **airing their** צריך שם עצם, והצירוף **a formal list of them** מחייב רבים, ולכן התשובה היא **grievances** (תלונות, טענות על יחס לא הוגן).
explanation.en: After **airing their** we need a noun, and **a formal list of them** needs a plural: **grievances** (complaints).

items.sentence: Had a pertinacious junior auditor not caught the error in time, the charity's tax-exempt status, and with it the trust of its donors, would have been seriously ________.

explanation.he: אחרי הצירוף **would have been seriously** צריך צורת **past participle**, ולכן משם העצם **jeopardy** בונים את הפועל **jeopardize** ומקבלים את הצורה **jeopardized** (הועמד בסכנה).
explanation.en: After **would have been seriously** we need a past participle, so **jeopardy** becomes **jeopardize**, then **jeopardized**.

items.sentence: Pacing backstage before her debut recital, the normally imperturbable young pianist ________ her hands so hard that her teacher reminded her she would soon need them.

explanation.he: בין הצירוף **young pianist** לבין הצירוף **her hands** צריך פועל בעבר, כמו הפועל **reminded**, ולכן הפועל הלא סדיר **wring** הופך לצורה **wrung** (פכרה את ידיה).
explanation.en: Between **young pianist** and **her hands** we need a past-tense verb, like **reminded**: irregular **wring** becomes **wrung**.

items.sentence: ________ by the success of its first small trial, the start-up launched its app in twelve countries at once, a leap that its chary investors had warned against.

explanation.he: בפתיחת המשפט, לפני הצירוף **by the success of its first small trial**, צריך צורת **past participle** באות גדולה, ולכן התשובה היא **Emboldened** (מעודדת, שקיבלה ביטחון).
explanation.en: Before **by the success of its first small trial** we need a capitalized past participle: **bold** gives **embolden**, so **Emboldened**.

items.sentence: Centuries before food science, cheesemakers insisted that a cheese's pungent flavor was ________ bound up with the meadows where the herd had grazed, a notion recent studies partly support.

explanation.he: לפני הצירוף **bound up with** צריך תואר פועל, והיצרנים טענו בתוקף (**insisted**) שאי אפשר להפריד בין הטעם למרעה, ולכן התשובה היא **inextricably** (באופן שאינו ניתן להפרדה).
explanation.en: Before **bound up with** we need an adverb, and the claim is that flavor and meadow cannot be separated: **inextricably**.

items.sentence: Openly ________ of amateur stargazers, the eminent astronomer and his acolytes refused even to glance through the retired teacher's telescope, and so missed the comet she had spotted first.

explanation.he: לפני מילת היחס **of** צריך שם תואר שמתאר יחס של בוז, כמו שהצירוף **refused even to glance** מראה, ולכן התשובה היא **contemptuous** (מזלזל, מלא בוז).
explanation.en: Before **of** we need an adjective showing scorn, as **refused even to glance** proves: **contemptuous**, not **contemptible**.

items.prompt: Would you rather watch a new movie at home or in a movie theater? Explain your choice.
items.highModel: I would much rather watch a new movie in a theater than at home. First, the experience is completely different. The screen is enormous and the sound surrounds you, so when I saw a riveting space adventure last winter, I felt as if I were flying with the astronauts. Second, going to the theater turns a movie into an event. My friends and I usually meet for pizza and then argue about the ending all the way home. It is true that tickets are expensive. However, I only go a few times a year, so the experience is worth the price. That is why I save the movies I care about most for the big screen.

rubricHigh.content: הבחירה מוצגת במשפט הראשון, בהשוואה בין שתי האפשרויות. יש שתי סיבות מפותחות, כל אחת עם דוגמה מהחיים (סרט מסוים, ערב עם חברים). הצד השני מוצג בהגינות (**It is true that …**) ומקבל מענה (**However, …**), ובסוף יש משפט סיכום.
rubricHigh.language: אין טעויות. המבנים מגוונים: מבנה העדפה (**would much rather … than**), פסוקית זמן בתוך משפט תוצאה (**so when I saw …, I felt as if …**) ומבנה של ויתור (**It is true that … However, …**). אוצר המילים מדויק ומתאר את החוויה (**enormous**, **surrounds**, **riveting**).

items.prompt: Should universities record every lecture and put it online, so that students can decide whether to attend in person? Explain your opinion.
items.highModel: In my view, universities should record every lecture and post it online. First, recordings make studying fairer. Many students work long hours or live far from campus, and missing one lecture should not cost them a whole topic. Second, recordings help even those who attend. When a lecturer explains a difficult idea too quickly, a student can replay that part until it finally makes sense. Admittedly, some students might stop coming to class and miss the impromptu conversations with lecturers and classmates that happen only on campus. However, this risk can be reduced if lectures include discussions and short tasks that a video cannot replace. On balance, recordings give students a safety net, not an excuse.

rubricHigh.content: העמדה מופיעה במשפט הראשון. יש שתי סיבות מפותחות, כל אחת עם תוצאה או מצב מוחשי מחיי הסטודנטים. הטענה הנגדית החזקה ביותר מוצגת בהגינות (**Admittedly, …**) ומקבלת מענה מעשי (**However, …**), ובסוף יש משפט סיכום.
rubricHigh.language: אין טעויות. המשפטים מורכבים ומגוונים: פסוקית זמן (**When a lecturer explains …**), סביל עם פועל מודלי (**can be reduced**), פסוקיות זיקה (**that a video cannot replace**) ומשפט תנאי (**if lectures include …**). אוצר המילים מדויק ואקדמי (**fairer**, **impromptu**, **a safety net**).

items.prompt: Some parents pay their children for doing chores at home, such as washing the dishes or taking out the trash. Is this a good idea, and why?
items.highModel: I do not think parents should pay children for ordinary chores. First, helping at home is part of family life. Parents are not paid for cooking dinner, so children should not expect money for clearing the table. Second, payment can change children's motives. A child who is paid to wash the dishes may start refusing to help without a reward, or even try to wheedle money out of their parents for every task. Admittedly, earning money teaches children how to save and spend it wisely. However, parents can give a fixed weekly allowance, which teaches the same lesson without turning the home into a business. Therefore, chores should remain a shared duty, not a paid job.

rubricHigh.content: העמדה מופיעה במשפט הראשון ומוגדרת במדויק (מטלות רגילות בבית). יש שתי סיבות מפותחות, אחת עם השוואה ואחת עם תוצאה. הטענה הנגדית מוצגת בהגינות (**Admittedly, …**), ובמענה מוצעת חלופה (**However, …**). בסוף יש משפט סיכום.
rubricHigh.language: אין טעויות. המשפטים מורכבים ומגוונים: סביל (**Parents are not paid**), פסוקית זיקה מגבילה (**A child who is paid …**) ופסוקית זיקה שמוסיפה מידע (**which teaches the same lesson**). אוצר המילים מדויק (**motives**, **allowance**, **wheedle**).

items.prompt: In many university courses, students complete projects in groups, and every member of the group receives the same grade. Is this a fair way to grade students, and why?
items.highModel: In my view, giving every member of a group the same grade is unfair, at least when it is the only grade. First, a shared grade lets some students shirk their share of the work. Last year, one member of my group skipped every meeting, leaving the onus of the report on the rest of us, yet he received the same 92. Second, a grade should tell employers what a particular student can do, which a shared grade cannot. Admittedly, teams at work also succeed or fail together. However, a manager sees people contribute every day, whereas a lecturer sees only the finished product. A fair system would therefore add an individual grade to the group one.

rubricHigh.content: העמדה ברורה כבר בפתיחה ומסויגת (**at least when …**). יש שתי סיבות עם תמיכה, הסתייגות הוגנת (**Admittedly …**) עם מענה מנומק (**However … whereas …**), וסיכום שמציע פתרון, למשל ציון קבוצתי לצד ציון אישי.
rubricHigh.language: אין טעויות. המשפטים מורכבים ומגוונים: מבנה מקוצר (**leaving the onus on …**), ניגוד בעזרת המילה **whereas** ופסוקיות זיקה. אוצר המילים מדויק בתחום הלימודים והעבודה בצוות.

items.prompt: Is it ever right to tell a small lie in order to spare someone's feelings? Explain your view.
items.highModel: I believe a small lie can be right, but only when the truth would hurt without helping. Suppose a friend asks whether you liked the dress she wore at her wedding. Since nothing can be changed, an unvarnished answer would merely wound her. Things change when the listener can still act on the answer. If the same friend were choosing a dress for an interview, a kind lie would deprive her of advice she needs. Admittedly, even small lies can erode trust once discovered. Yet a brusque verdict on something trivial probably damages a friendship more than a gentle fiction ever could. Only when the truth can still be useful, then, does honesty become a duty.

rubricHigh.content: העמדה מסויגת ומבוססת על תנאי מדויק (**only when …**). שתי דוגמאות מנוגדות בודקות את התנאי, יש הסתייגות (**Admittedly …**) ומענה זהיר עליה (**Yet … probably …**), והסיכום חוזר לתנאי.
rubricHigh.language: אין טעויות. התחביר מתקדם וטבעי: היפוך סדר המילים (**Only when … does …**), משפט תנאי דמיוני (**If the same friend were choosing …**) ומילות סייג (**probably**). אוצר המילים מדויק ועשיר.

items.prompt: Many people read online reviews and star ratings before they buy a product or choose a restaurant. Do such reviews really help people make better choices, and why?
items.highModel: Online reviews do help, though far less than their star ratings suggest. Their real value lies in patterns. When dozens of guests independently complain that a hotel's walls are thin, the complaint is almost certainly true, and no advertisement would ever have admitted it. Ratings, by contrast, are easily distorted. Seldom does a satisfied customer bother to write, so the loudest voices tend to be disgruntled ones. Worse, some businesses pay for laudatory comments. Admittedly, even a distorted average can warn us away from a truly bad product. However, it cannot tell us whether a restaurant suits our own taste. Reviews, then, are most useful to those who ignore the stars and read for recurring details.

rubricHigh.content: העמדה קובעת כבר בפתיחה עד כמה הביקורות עוזרות. יש הבחנה מנומקת בין מה שעוזר (תלונות שחוזרות) לבין מה שמטעה (הדירוג), הסתייגות (**Admittedly …**) ומענה עליה (**However …**), וסיכום שמגדיר למי הביקורות מועילות.
rubricHigh.language: אין טעויות. התחביר מתקדם וטבעי: היפוך סדר המילים (**Seldom does …**), ניגוד (**by contrast**) ומילות סייג (**almost certainly**, **tend to**). אוצר המילים מדויק ועשיר.

items.title: Why Bread Goes Stale
paragraphs: Fresh bread is soft and springy, but after a day or two on the kitchen counter, it turns hard and dry in the mouth. Most people assume that a stale loaf has simply become desiccated, meaning that its water has escaped into the air. This explanation sounds reasonable, yet it tells only a small part of the story.

The main cause of staling lies in starch, the substance that makes up most of the flour in bread. During baking, heat and water loosen the tiny grains of starch, which swell and become soft. As the bread cools, however, the starch slowly returns to a hard, ordered form. This change makes the inside of the loaf firm and crumbly even when no water is lost. In fact, bread kept in a sealed plastic bag still goes stale.

Temperature plays a large part in this process. Starch hardens fastest when it is cool but not frozen, so bread stored in a refrigerator goes stale several times faster than bread left at room temperature. In a freezer, by contrast, the change nearly stops, which is why frozen bread can taste almost fresh weeks later.

Staling can also be reversed, at least for a short time. Heating a stale slice in a hot oven loosens the starch again, and the bread becomes soft once more. The effect does not last, though. As soon as the bread cools, it hardens again, often faster than before, partly because some of its water has now been lost in the heat.

glossary.he: מיובש לגמרי, שכל הלחות יצאה ממנו
glossary.en: completely dried out

questions.stem: What is the main purpose of the passage?
options: To warn readers not to keep bread in the refrigerator
To show that bread goes stale mainly because its water slowly escapes into the air around it
To explain the real cause of staling and how temperature and heat affect it
To describe the many ways in which foods change as they grow older

explanation.he: המשפט **The main cause of staling lies in starch** (הסיבה העיקרית להתיישנות היא העמילן) ופסקאות 3–4 על קור וחום מראים שהמטרה היא להסביר מה באמת גורם ללחם להתיישן.
explanation.en: The sentence **The main cause of staling lies in starch** and the paragraphs on cold and heat show that the passage explains what really makes bread stale.

questions.stem: According to paragraph 2, why does bread in a sealed plastic bag still go stale?
options: Water escapes slowly through the bag into the air.
Its starch grains swell and grow soft as the bread cools.
Its starch grains were not loosened enough during baking.
Its starch hardens although the bread keeps its water.

explanation.he: בפסקה 2 נאמר שהעמילן מתקשה גם כשלא אובדים מים (הצירוף **even when no water is lost**), ולכן גם לחם בשקית סגורה מתיישן.
explanation.en: Paragraph 2 says the starch hardens **even when no water is lost**, so a sealed bag cannot stop staling.

questions.stem: According to paragraph 3, why does bread go stale faster in a refrigerator than at room temperature?
options: The cold, dry air inside a refrigerator slowly draws the water out of the bread.
Its starch hardens most quickly in cold conditions above freezing.
The water inside the loaf turns to ice.
Bread at room temperature is usually eaten sooner.

explanation.he: המילה **so** בפסקה 3 מחברת סיבה לתוצאה: העמילן מתקשה הכי מהר כשהוא קר אבל לא קפוא (הצירוף **cool but not frozen**), ולכן לחם במקרר מתיישן מהר יותר.
explanation.en: The word **so** links cause and effect: starch hardens fastest when it is **cool but not frozen**, and a refrigerator keeps bread exactly that way.

questions.stem: The word "reversed" in paragraph 4 is closest in meaning to
options: undone
slowed down
made worse
repeated

explanation.he: אחרי המילה **reversed** בא ההסבר **the bread becomes soft once more** (הלחם נעשה רך שוב), ולכן המשמעות היא בוטל, הוחזר לקדמותו (**undone**).
explanation.en: The next sentence, **the bread becomes soft once more**, shows that **reversed** means undone.

questions.stem: What can be inferred from paragraph 4 about heating stale bread?
options: It keeps the bread soft for several days afterward.
It puts back the water that the bread lost while it was stored.
It may be the best way to store bread for a long time.
It is most useful just before the bread is going to be eaten.

explanation.he: לפי פסקה 4 הרכות לא נשמרת (המשפט **The effect does not last**) והלחם מתקשה כשהוא מתקרר (הצירוף **As soon as the bread cools**), ולכן כדאי לחמם אותו רק רגע לפני האכילה.
explanation.en: Since **The effect does not last** and the bread hardens **As soon as the bread cools**, heating helps most right before eating.

items.title: Selling Winter: The Rise and Fall of the Ice Trade
paragraphs: Before electric refrigerators, keeping food cold in summer was a luxury that few could afford. In the early 1800s, however, a few merchants in New England saw an opportunity in something their region had plenty of: winter ice. They planned to cut blocks from frozen lakes and ship them to warm ports far away. Many observers derided the scheme as foolish, predicting that the cargo would turn to water long before it arrived.

At first, the critics appeared to be vindicated. Early shipments lost much of their ice to melting, and the business lost money for years. Gradually, though, the traders learned to protect their cargo. They packed the blocks tightly, since a solid mass of ice melts more slowly than separate pieces, and covered them with sawdust, a cheap waste product of local lumber mills that helped keep out the heat. Thick-walled storehouses at both ends of the voyage reduced losses further.

With these methods in place, the trade grew rapidly. By mid-century, ice from New England was reaching the Caribbean, South America and even India, while at home a steady supply let families keep iceboxes and let fresh meat and fish travel farther. Costs stayed low. The ice itself cost almost nothing to produce; the main expenses were the labor of cutting it and the price of transport. Even transport cost less than one might expect, because many ships sailing south would otherwise have carried little cargo, so their owners were glad to fill the empty space at low rates.

The trade did not last, however. Late in the century, ice-making machines began to spread, offering advantages that natural ice could not match. Their output did not depend on the weather, so a mild winter no longer meant a summer shortage. Moreover, as cities and factories grew, many lakes became polluted, and buyers increasingly worried about the cleanliness of ice cut from them. By the time electric refrigerators reached most homes, the business of selling winter had all but disappeared.

glossary.en: laughed at or spoke of with contempt
shown to have been right

questions.stem: Which of the following best expresses the main idea of the passage?
options: A trade that critics called foolish soon collapsed, since most of its ice melted long before it arrived.
A trade that many expected to fail did well for decades until machines took its place.
Sawdust and tightly packed blocks made it possible to ship ice over long distances.
Keeping food cold has been a problem for people in many places and periods.

explanation.he: הקטע עובר מהלעג לתוכנית (הצירוף **derided the scheme as foolish**), דרך הצמיחה של הסחר (הצירוף **the trade grew rapidly**) ועד הדעיכה שלו (המשפט **The trade did not last**), והתשובה הנכונה מכסה את שלושת השלבים.
explanation.en: The passage moves from doubt (**derided the scheme as foolish**) to success (**the trade grew rapidly**) to decline (**The trade did not last**).

questions.stem: According to the passage, why did the traders pack the blocks of ice tightly together?

items.title: Built for Sound: Why Concert Halls Differ
paragraphs: Anyone who has heard the same music in a school gym and in a fine concert hall knows that a room is far from a neutral container for sound. Every surface reflects part of the sound striking it, so a listener hears a mixture of direct sound and countless delayed reflections. The way these reflections build up and die away, known as reverberation, largely determines how a room sounds. Yet not until about 1900 did designers have a reliable method for predicting it; builders had hitherto relied on copying admired older halls, with uneven results.

The ideal amount of reverberation depends on what a room is for. Speech calls for a short reverberation time, since each syllable must fade before the next one arrives; otherwise the sounds overlap and words become hard to follow. A lecture hall therefore aims for limpid sound, even at some cost to warmth. Orchestral music, by contrast, generally benefits from longer reverberation, which blends successive notes into a fullness that listeners tend to call warm.

Reverberation also depends on a room's materials. Hard surfaces such as plaster and concrete reflect most of the sound striking them, whereas curtains and carpets absorb much of it. Among the most absorbent elements in any hall is the audience itself, since clothing and bodies take in sound much as curtains do. As a result, the difference between an empty hall and a full one can be pronounced. To limit this difference, many halls are fitted with padded seats designed to absorb roughly as much sound as a seated listener would.

Shape matters as well. Many musicians and acousticians admire tall, narrow halls on a rectangular plan, often called shoeboxes. In such rooms, much of the reflected sound reaches listeners from the side walls, and these side reflections seem to surround the audience, giving the music a sonorous, enveloping quality. Wider halls, which can seat more people, tend to weaken this effect, a compromise that designers of large modern halls have tried to soften with angled wall panels.

items.title: Talking Across Valleys: The World's Whistled Languages
paragraphs: On a few steep islands and in certain mountain valleys, people have long conversed by whistling across distances that would defeat the loudest shout. To the uninitiated, such exchanges may sound like birdsong or like the simple signals used to call a dog. Far from being a mere set of signals, however, whistled speech is an ordinary spoken language transposed into whistles: in principle, a whistler can say anything the spoken language can, and a native speaker who has learned the technique can follow it.

The advantage is largely physical. A whistle concentrates its energy in a narrow band of pitches above most natural background noise, so it remains intelligible at distances over which a shouted word would blur into an indistinct cry. Under favorable conditions, whistled messages have reportedly been understood several kilometers away. Unsurprisingly, the practice has arisen chiefly where rugged terrain or dense forest makes travel slow, and where shepherds and farmers working alone need to reach one another.

How a language is whistled depends on its sound system. In tonal languages, where the pitch of a syllable can change a word's meaning, whistlers mainly reproduce the melody of the tones; in other languages, they imitate the way the voice shifts from vowel to vowel, rendering consonants as brief breaks or slides. Either way, the whistle carries a denuded version of speech, stripped of much of its detail. Seldom can a single whistled word be identified in isolation, so listeners lean heavily on context, a skill in which those raised with the practice from childhood far outstrip adult learners.

In recent decades, roads and mobile phones have removed much of the need for whistling, and several whistled forms are now moribund, kept up by a few older speakers and rarely passed on. Yet decline is not inevitable. On at least one island, the local whistled form has become a school subject. Whether such efforts can restore whistling to daily use, rather than preserving it as a cherished emblem of local identity, remains to be seen.
